findings.title: remove() now unconditionally calls the backend delegate, defeating the cache
findings.body: In remove(String alias), `IdentityProviderModel storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias);` is now executed unconditionally before checking cache validity. Previously, the delegate (JPA) lookup only happened when `isInvalid(cacheKey)` was true; when the cache entry was valid, the code used the already-cached `CachedIdentityProvider` via `realmCache.getCache().get(cacheKey, ...)` without hitting the backend. With this change, every call to remove() now performs an extra backend lookup even in the common case where the idp is already cached and valid, which is a performance regression that partially defeats the purpose of this caching layer. The fetched `storedIdp` is only actually needed for the `registerIDPLoginInvalidation` call and for the (already-existing) invalid-cache branch; it should be computed lazily/only when needed instead of unconditionally up front.

findings.title: Cleanup uses a hard-coded wrong alias, so created IdPs are never removed
findings.body: In the new testCacheIDPForLogin test, cleanups are registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` (lines 381 and 425), using the literal string "alias" instead of the actual alias that was just created (e.g. "idp-alias-" + i, or "idp-alias-20"). As a result, the cleanup callback attempts to delete a non-existent identity provider named "alias" instead of the ones created by the test, so the 20+ identity providers created in this test are never actually removed after the test runs. This can leak test data across test executions/tests in the suite (the same organization "orga"/"orgb" are reused by other tests in this class) and may also cause cleanup-time failures (404 on delete) that mask the real test result.
